title: Standard Error
prompt:
A sample of n = 49 observations has population σ = 23.

Find the standard error SE = σ/√n as an exact fraction.
hint: SE = σ/√n; √n is exact since n is a perfect square
recap: The standard error of the mean is SE = σ/√n: the sample mean's spread shrinks with √n, so quadrupling n halves the SE.
